luc_001: You can recognise it by its foliage held in flat horizontal plates, so the crown reads as dark tiers rather than a dome. It stands as the Orto Botanico di Lucca's symbol, its patriarch tree.
luc_002: You can recognise it by its height, 35 metres, taller than any tower but the two you can climb, with soft, fibrous bark. It stands in the Orto Botanico di Lucca, a second redwood 40 metres away.
luc_004: You can recognise it by standing atop the old gun platform on the city walls, evergreen and unchanged through the seasons. It stands on the Baluardo San Regolo, Mura Urbane.
luc_005: You can recognise them by growing kept small in a brick planter atop a medieval tower, dense and shrub-sized rather than full height. They stand on the roof of the Torre Guinigi.
luc_006: You can recognise it by its trunk, 7 metres round, the largest registered in the whole municipality. It stands in the Garden of the Righteous at Villa Bottini.
luc_007: You can recognise it by its single, clean, straight stem with branches in loose whorls, standing tall rather than wide. It stands in the Orto Botanico, two minutes from the cedar.
luc_008: You can recognise it by its dark, glossy leaves with rust-brown undersides that flash in the wind, and cream flowers up to 30cm wide in May and June. It stands on Via dell'Orto Botanico.
luc_009: You can recognise it by growing right on the bank of the open canal running down the middle of the street. It stands on Via del Fosso.
luc_010: You can recognise it by leaves with a pale, blue-grey underside that flickers in the wind, the larger of the city's two camphor trees. It stands on Via Barsanti e Matteucci, outside the walls.
luc_011: You can recognise it by its trunk, 4.88 metres round, the thickest plane in the city and one of only three registered trees on the whole wall circuit. It stands near Porta San Donato.
